Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself to break the task down into smaller, more manageable pieces. Think of it like looking up a word in a dictionary, only to find that the definition uses another word you do not know, so you have to look that one up too. To prevent the function from calling itself forever and crashing the program, it must have a base case that tells it when to stop. Once the base case is reached, the function finishes its work and passes the answers back up the chain until the original problem is completely solved.
